idiom_name: Slick Table + row case class per concrete class; ++ (unionAll) for hierarchy reads
implementation_notes: Slick maps one case class to one Table definition, so the concrete-table hierarchy is written as one Table/row pair per concrete class with the shared columns repeated in each row type, and Slick's ++ (unionAll) concatenates queries with compatible column lists for a mixed read. There is no inheritance mapping to configure and no discriminator to maintain, which is why this is idiomatic rather than library-provided; the JPA route (Hibernate's TABLE_PER_CLASS through Java interop) stays available when the team already runs a Jakarta Persistence stack. Prefer this when most queries are per concrete type; use joined inheritance or a view when hierarchy-wide queries dominate.
pitfalls: Slick requires both sides of ++ to have the same column types and count, so a mixed read must project to a common shape and pad missing columns - a code-level contract, not a schema-level one.
Shared columns live in every row case class and Table definition, so renaming a field is a multi-file change with no compiler link between the tables.
Slick does not generate keys across tables: per-table auto-increment columns collide in a union, so use a shared sequence or UUID.
